Skills

Extend your deep agent's capabilities with portable skill definitions.

graph TD Skill[Skill Definition] --> SKILL[SKILL.md] Skill --> Scripts[Optional Scripts] Skill --> Assets[Optional Assets] Agent[Deep Agent] -->|Loads| Skill Agent -->|Executes| Instructions[Instructions from SKILL.md] Agent -->|Uses| Tools[Tools/Scripts]

What are skills?

A skill is a directory containing:

  • SKILL.md: The main instruction file with YAML frontmatter.
  • Scripts: Helper scripts (optional).
  • Resources: Templates or assets (optional).

Example SKILL.md

The SKILL.md file defines the skill's metadata and instructions.

View Example SKILL.md 
---
name: langgraph-docs
description: Use this skill for requests related to LangGraph in order to fetch relevant documentation to provide accurate, up-to-date guidance.
---
# langgraph-docs

## Overview
This skill explains how to access LangGraph Python documentation to help answer questions and guide implementation.

## Instructions
### 1. Fetch the Documentation Index
Use the fetch_url tool to read the following URL: https://docs.langchain.com/llms.txt
This provides a structured list of all available documentation with descriptions.

### 2. Select Relevant Documentation
Based on the question, identify 2-4 most relevant documentation URLs from the index.
Prioritize:
- Specific how-to guides for implementation questions
- Core concept pages for understanding questions
- Tutorials for end-to-end examples
- Reference docs for API details

### 3. Fetch Selected Documentation
Use the fetch_url tool to read the selected documentation URLs.

### 4. Provide Accurate Guidance
After reading the documentation, complete the user's request.

Usage

You can load skills into an agent by pointing to their directory paths. How you load them depends on your storage backend.

1. Using StateBackend (Default)

When using the default StateBackend, files are ephemeral. You must "seed" the skills into the agent's virtual filesystem at runtime.

StateBackend Example 
from urllib.request import urlopen
from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

checkpointer = MemorySaver()

# Fetch the skill content
skill_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langchain-ai/deepagentsjs/refs/heads/main/examples/skills/langgraph-docs/SKILL.md"
with urlopen(skill_url) as response:
    skill_content = response.read().decode('utf-8')

# Define the file structure to seed
skills_files = {
    "/skills/langgraph-docs/SKILL.md": skill_content
}

agent = create_deep_agent(
    skills=["./skills/"], # Tell agent where to look in its virtual FS
    checkpointer=checkpointer,
)

result = agent.invoke(
    {
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is langgraph?"}],
        # Seed the files here
        "files": skills_files 
    },
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "12345"}},
)

2. Using StoreBackend

If using a persistent StoreBackend (like Postgres or InMemoryStore), you can pre-load skills into the store once, and they will differ per user/thread only if namespaced.

StoreBackend Example 
from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend
from langgraph.store.memory import InMemoryStore

store = InMemoryStore()

# Pre-load skill into the store
store.put(
    namespace=("filesystem",),
    key="/skills/langgraph-docs/SKILL.md",
    value=skill_content
)

agent = create_deep_agent(
    backend=(lambda rt: StoreBackend(rt)), # Use StoreBackend
    store=store,
    skills=["./skills/"]
)

3. Using FilesystemBackend (Local Dev)

For agents running locally with access to your real disk, use FilesystemBackend. This is great for development or CLI tools.

FilesystemBackend Example 
from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from deepagents.backends.filesystem import FilesystemBackend
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

checkpointer = MemorySaver()

agent = create_deep_agent(
    # Point to a real directory on your disk
    backend=FilesystemBackend(root_dir="/Users/user/my-project"),
    # Skills are loaded from disk relative to root_dir
    skills=["/Users/user/my-project/skills/"],
    interrupt_on={
        "write_file": True, 
        "edit_file": True 
    },
    checkpointer=checkpointer,
)

When to use skills vs tools

Skills
  • Use when there is a lot of context (docs, guidelines) that would bloat the system prompt.
  • Use to bundle capabilities definitions + instructions + assets.
  • Use for complex multi-step procedures that need their own "SOP".
Tools
  • Use for atomic actions (API calls, simple calculations).
  • Use when instructions are simple enough for the main system prompt.
  • Use when the agent does not have access to a filesystem.
